boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study settings inside Hope College’s Van Wylen Library, spanning quiet floors, collaborative areas, specialized labs and reservable rooms.

cards.title: Lower-Level Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Quiet study near science, technology and language collections
cards.notes: Head downstairs for quiet work near the P–PT and Q–Z stacks; use a group room when discussion is necessary and keep shared-floor noise low.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library level pairing broad subject collections with enclosed group-study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies the Van Wylen Library lower level as a quiet zone with group study rooms and collections covering literature, languages, science, nursing, medicine and technology.
cards.source_title: Map of the Lower Level | Library
cards.access_notes: Use during Van Wylen Library’s current open hours. Group study rooms are for Hope College students, available first come, first served or by advance reservation.

cards.title: Main-Floor Collaboration Zone
cards.subtitle: Reference tools, current reading and academic help nearby
cards.notes: Set up here for a collaborative assignment, then use the Research Help Desk or Klooster writing assistants when the work calls for focused support.
cards.short_summary: A social work area with reference materials and research and writing assistance close at hand.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College describes the main floor as a place for collaborative work and socializing, with reference sources, current magazines, the Research Help Desk and Klooster writing assistance.
cards.source_title: Map of the Main Floor | Library
cards.access_notes: Use during current library hours. Writing assistance is offered through the Klooster Center, and librarian help is available at the Research Help Desk.

cards.title: Second-Floor Collaboration Zone
cards.subtitle: Art and music stacks beside specialized library spaces
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from conversation, then consult the nearby M, N and PZ collections or shift into one of the floor’s specialized rooms.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative floor anchored by arts collections and several project-oriented library facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College calls the second floor a place for collaborative work and socializing and locates the Curriculum Library, Digital Media Lab, Granberg Room and Library Teaching Lab there.
cards.source_title: Map of the Second Floor | Library
cards.access_notes: Use during current Van Wylen Library hours. Individual specialized rooms on this floor may have separate reservation or use requirements.

cards.title: Third-Floor Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Low-noise study near social-science collections
cards.notes: Choose this floor for quiet reading in history, economics, sociology, politics or education; move into a group room when collaboration begins.
cards.short_summary: A quiet floor with social-science stacks and group rooms for contained conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies the third floor as a quiet zone with group study rooms and collections including history, geography, economics, sociology, political science, law and education.
cards.source_title: Map of the Third Floor | Library
cards.access_notes: Use during current library hours. Observe quiet-zone expectations; Hope says study rooms are not soundproof and conversations should remain low.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Quiet work among humanities collections
cards.notes: Climb to this quiet floor for reading or drafting near philosophy, psychology, religion and world-history stacks; use a group room for discussion.
cards.short_summary: A top-floor quiet zone surrounded by humanities books and equipped with group-study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies the fourth floor as a quiet zone with group study rooms and collections in philosophy, psychology, religion and world history.
cards.source_title: Map of the Fourth Floor | Library
cards.access_notes: Use during current Van Wylen Library hours. Follow quiet-zone expectations and reserve a group study room in advance when needed.

cards.title: A.J. Muste Alcove
cards.subtitle: Second-floor study alcove with Hope-alumni sculpture
cards.notes: Settle into the dedicated alcove for individual work, and pause to examine the Muste bust and John Saurer’s chalkboard-surfaced sculpture.
cards.short_summary: A named study alcove where focused work shares space with two alumni-made artworks.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College documents the A.J. Muste Alcove as a second-floor study alcove featuring John Saurer’s interactive sculpture “Stop, Look, and Listen” and Ryan Dodde II’s bust of Muste.
cards.access_notes: Located on Van Wylen Library’s second floor and usable during current library hours; the official page lists no reservation requirement for the alcove.

cards.title: Digital Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Technology-equipped workspace for multimedia projects
cards.notes: Bring media-heavy assignments here for specialized software, collaborative workspace and peer guidance; confirm support availability before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A project workspace for editing, visualization, fabrication and other technology-intensive coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College says the Digital Media Lab provides peer consultants, specialized computers and software, collaborative workspaces, a Sound Room, Cricut access and a heat press.
cards.access_notes: The lab is on Van Wylen Library’s second floor and serves students and staff. Check the library’s current hours and DML support schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Curriculum Library
cards.subtitle: Second-floor room beside education-focused resources
cards.notes: Use this named room when coursework benefits from the second floor’s education setting; submit an EMS request before relying on exclusive access.
cards.short_summary: A reservable second-floor library room suited to coursework connected with curriculum resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College lists the Curriculum Library among Van Wylen Library’s reservable rooms and places it on the second floor.
cards.access_notes: Submit a reservation request through Hope’s Event Management System. Availability and approval are not guaranteed; also verify current library hours.

cards.title: Granberg Room 222
cards.subtitle: Reservable second-floor library classroom
cards.notes: Plan this room for structured group work that needs a classroom setup; check EMS first and use the outside tablet only for an eligible same-day opening.
cards.short_summary: A reservable library classroom for organized collaborative sessions rather than drop-in individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies Granberg Room 222 as one of Van Wylen Library’s two classrooms and permits same-day reservations through the Quick Reserve tablet, with other requests routed through EMS.
cards.access_notes: Same-day reservations may be made on the Quick Reserve tablet outside the room. Other reservations require an EMS request and library approval; September and early October restrictions apply.

cards.title: Library Teaching Lab 202
cards.subtitle: Reservable classroom for computer-supported group work
cards.notes: Choose the LTL when a study session needs a classroom and computers; request it through EMS or check the door tablet for same-day availability.
cards.short_summary: A reservable teaching lab designed for library instruction and computer-related group sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies Library Teaching Lab 202 as a library classroom used for library and computer-related instruction, with same-day Quick Reserve and advance EMS request options.
cards.access_notes: Same-day use requires an available Quick Reserve slot; other requests need EMS submission and library approval. The room is restricted during September and the first week of October.
